name: Primary Short Bowel Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Short Bowel Syndrome

criteria.description: Anatomical loss or congenital absence of significant portions of the small intestine resulting in malabsorption
Evidence of chronic malnutrition or nutrient deficiencies despite adequate oral intake
Radiological confirmation of shortened small bowel length via imaging studies (e.g., contrast studies, MRI)
Exclusion of secondary causes such as surgical resection or inflammatory bowel disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (anatomical loss, malabsorption, and radiological confirmation) with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including gastroenterology and radiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by chronic diarrhea and steatorrhea

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked reduction in small intestinal length
searchTerms: marked reduction in small bowel size

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K
abdominal pain with gas and swelling

occasional.notes: May cause additional malabsorption and systemic symptoms

occasional.symptomName: Osteopenia or osteoporosis secondary to vitamin D deficiency
searchTerms: weakened bones from vitamin D deficiency
osteopenia or osteoporosis secondary to low vitamin D

rare.symptomName: Cholestasis or liver dysfunction secondary to long-term parenteral nutrition
rare.notes: Though hepatic is not a valid bodySystem per schema, this is a known complication; omitted from systemsAffected
searchTerms: liver problems from long-term IV nutrition

rare.symptomName: Thromboembolic events related to central venous catheter use
searchTerms: blood clots related to central venous catheters

laboratory: Low serum albumin and total protein
Vitamin A, D, E, K deficiencies
Elevated liver enzymes in parenteral nutrition-associated liver disease
imaging: Radiological evidence of shortened small bowel length on contrast studies
MRI enterography showing reduced absorptive surface
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified for primary short bowel syndrome
other: Dependence on parenteral nutrition for caloric and nutrient support
Histological evidence of mucosal adaptation or atrophy in small intestine biopsies

distinguishingFeatures: History of surgical resection or trauma
Underlying inflammatory bowel disease or ischemic injury
Normal small bowel length on imaging
Steatorrhea without anatomical loss of intestine

redFlags: Progressive liver dysfunction in parenteral nutrition-dependent patients
references: Crenn P, Messing B. Short bowel syndrome: epidemiology and etiology. Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol. 2006;20(3):461-473.
